mechanism_narrative: Lower federal funds rate levels below 4.0% signal accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signal broad demand contraction that reduces corporate revenue expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing supply chain disruption that increases inflationary pressures and reduces corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High employment levels (PAYEMS above 159,000 thousand) signal strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 159,000 thousand, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate increases (UNRATE) and employment declines (PAYEMS) signal labor market deterioration that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS declines from prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Residential construction permits below 1,350 thousand units signal housing demand slowdown that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST is below 1350, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
